To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have proposed a new subset selection procedure for the selection of the population having the largest mean lifetime when the guarantee times are the same, and (ii) for the case of k = 2 exponential populations, we have established that the proposed procedure is minimax, among procedures that satisfy the P*-condition, for the loss measured by size of the selected set.
the proposed selection procedure is monotonic for a general k and minimax for the case of k = 2.
a new subset selection procedure for selecting the population having longest mean lifetime is proposed, the procedure is monotone in general, and the procedure is minimax for k = 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the subset selection formulation of selecting the population with the longest mean lifetime when the guarantee times are the same.
the problem of subset selection in the context of selecting the population that has the longest mean lifetime when the guarantee times are the same.
the problem of selecting the exponential population having the longest lifetime when the guarantee times are the same.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed procedure is minimax for a general k, under the loss measured by size of the selected set, and for k = 2 and under the loss measured either by size of the set or by the loss measured by probability of selecting the best population.
the proposed subset procedure has a good chance of selecting the population with the longest mean lifetime.
the proposed subset procedure is the best selection procedure among all the selection procedures for the goal of subset selection of the best population, under the P*-condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed subset procedure is monotone and minimax for k = 2.
we have proposed a selection procedure which is minimax for the loss measured by size of the selected subsets for k = 2 and monotone for general k (≥2).
the proposed subset procedure is monotone (for a general k), minimax (for k = 2) and has a high probability of inclusion of the best (longest mean lifetime) population in the selected set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed subset procedure is a monotone procedure and, for k = 2 only, it is minimax under the P*-condition.
the subset selection formulation is a natural way to formulate selection problems in which the goal is to select the “best” of a set of populations having the same guarantee time.
the proposed subset procedure is monotone, minimax and is easy to implement.
